# Question: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Strongest identified rival: per-color envelope expansion

For each nonzero color in a row, paint the originally-zero cell immediately
before its leftmost occurrence and immediately after its rightmost occurrence.
Do not grow inner boundaries of disconnected occurrences of that same color.
This substitutes two per-color extrema for recognition of every maximal run.
It is a particularly strong rival because every original generated row has at
most one run of each color. On that domain the rival and correct rule are
identical by construction, not merely by the finite census. Both also match
all three canonical training pairs and the stored test pair exactly.

An actual unforced version-2.1.0 draw, seed **4**, sample_index **0**,
difficulty **None**, overrides **{}**, provides this six-by-seven input.
Each line below is one grid row; 0 is the literal background.

Input:
```
0000000
0000000
0000000
0777770
0050050
0000000
```

Actual canonical Racket output:
```
0000000
0000000
0000000
7777777
0555555
0000000
```

Color-envelope rival output:
```
0000000
0000000
0000000
7777777
0550055
0000000
```

The two inward flank cells at zero-based coordinates (4,3) and (4,4) must turn
from zero to 5. The rival leaves both zero. This is not a label conjecture:
`workspace/shortcut_probe.py` invokes the canonical `program_solution` through
`RacketBridge` and `wrap_rule`, and compares the rival to that actual result.
The case is preserved verbatim in `checks/shortcut-after.json` under
`witnesses.color_envelope`, with full draw parameters and source hashes, and
in `checks/shortcut-after.jsonl`.

The revised generator emits these cases both by ordinary default draws
(**76/512** in the recorded plan) and via the exact public override
`scene_profile="repeated_color"`. Every one of its **64** forced boundary cases
was a verified counterexample. The original default census found **0/512**,
and inspection establishes exclusion throughout its constructed domain.

## A second independently exposed rival

Process only the first two maximal horizontal runs in each row, ignoring all
later runs. This also matches every canonical pair and the original domain,
which constructs at most two same-row runs.

Actual unforced version-2.1.0 draw: seed **22**, sample_index **0**,
difficulty **None**, overrides **{}**.

Input:
```
000000000
000000000
006070880
000000000
```

Actual Racket output:
```
000000000
000000000
066778888
000000000
```

First-two-runs rival:
```
000000000
000000000
066777880
000000000
```

Here the third run must own the shared gap immediately before it and grow into
its right flank. The revised `three_runs` profile guarantees a visible third
right flank even when gaps differ. Recorded default refutations are **44/512**;
forced profile-boundary refutations are **64/64**. The exact case and both
outputs are in `witnesses.first_two_runs` in the same JSON report.

## Verification and claim boundary

Both rivals were evaluated against all four stored canonical pairs: neither
had a disagreement. The before/after probe also verifies canonical Racket
labels against stored outputs, generated-grid validation/replay, and mirror
parity. The final shared strict semantic gate independently verifies declared
witness/rival relationships: 57 color-envelope and 57 first-two-run witnesses
across 600 scheduled draws, with no failed claim.

These are the strongest plausible shortcuts identified here, not a theorem
that no stronger competitor exists. Singleton omission is another
canonical-equivalent rival, but the baseline already countered it frequently.
No arbitrary learner was trained, and a random short lesson can still omit
both newly distinguishing profile families. Distribution-level coverage is
not a per-lesson guarantee.
